portInfo.description: Port of Nordfjordeid sits at the head of Eidsfjord in Vestland and markets a rural fjord call between Bergen and Ålesund. Larger ships (port text: 150 m+) typically use the SeaWalk — a foldable floating walkway the docking procedure says can serve ships up to 340 m and up to 7000 passengers between mooring buoys — while other calls tender; once at the dock the guest flow is described as identical. The terminal building holds souvenir shop, toilets, tourist/excursion desk and port security. Confirm SeaWalk vs tender on the daily programme before timing Sagastad. Gangway GPS pins remain null.

climate.description: Oceanic climate with cool summers and cold winters

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

topThings: Sagastad Viking Centre — 10–15 min walk; opens on cruise days — ~60–120 min.
Eidsgata / wooden-house centre + grave mounds on the Sagastad recommended route — ~45–90 min.
Regional Loen Skylift / Briksdal — only with line-confirmed coaches and large buffers; minutes not verified here.
thingsToDo.shortCall: ≥4 h. Exit/SeaWalk 30 + Sagastad 90 + centre 30 + return 30 + 75 min buffer ≈ 255 — tight; drop centre loop if SeaWalk queues.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Ask the ship whether you are on SeaWalk or tender before locking Sagastad timing.
